evals.name: urgent-open-filter
evals.prompt: You are working in an existing TypeScript project (a helpdesk backend) that uses @faceteer/facet with DynamoDB Local already running on localhost:8000. Read README.md and src/facets.ts first. Implement src/urgent.ts exporting `getUrgentOpenTickets(orgId: string): Promise<Ticket[]>` that returns ALL tickets with status 'open' and priority 5 for the org. Then run `npx tsx setup-table.ts` and `npx tsx seed.ts`, and write and run demo-urgent.ts that prints the ticketIds returned for org 'acme'. Typecheck with `npx tsc --noEmit`.
assertions: Demo output contains exactly the ticket ids t024, t099, t174, t249 (all four, nothing else)
If a filter expression is used, pagination loops while a cursor is returned (never stops on an empty or short page); a per-status GSI query with a cursor loop is equally acceptable
npx tsc --noEmit passes in the sandbox

evals.name: tickets-from-id
evals.prompt: You are working in an existing TypeScript project (a helpdesk backend) that uses @faceteer/facet with DynamoDB Local already running on localhost:8000. Read README.md and src/facets.ts first. Implement src/from-id.ts exporting `getTicketsFromId(orgId: string, fromTicketId: string): Promise<Ticket[]>` that returns every ticket whose ticketId is lexicographically >= fromTicketId (ticket ids are zero-padded so lexicographic order is id order). Then run `npx tsx setup-table.ts` and `npx tsx seed.ts`, and write and run demo-from.ts that prints the count and first/last ticketId for getTicketsFromId('acme', 't250'). Typecheck with `npx tsc --noEmit`.
assertions: Demo output shows exactly 50 tickets, from t250 to t299
The key condition is bounded (between, or an explicit upper bound / prefix strategy) rather than a bare unbounded greaterThanOrEqual left in the shipped code
The function does not crash on non-ticket rows sharing the partition (watcher records)
npx tsc --noEmit passes in the sandbox

evals.name: latest-ticket
evals.prompt: You are working in an existing TypeScript project (a helpdesk backend) that uses @faceteer/facet with DynamoDB Local already running on localhost:8000. Read README.md and src/facets.ts first. Implement src/latest.ts exporting `getMostRecentTicket(orgId: string): Promise<Ticket | null>` that returns the single ticket with the greatest createdAt in the org. Then run `npx tsx setup-table.ts` and `npx tsx seed.ts`, and write and run demo-latest.ts that prints the ticketId and createdAt of the result for org 'acme'. Typecheck with `npx tsc --noEmit`.
assertions: Demo output shows ticketId t227 (createdAt 2026-06-13T11:00:00.000Z), not t299 or any other id

The implementation queries a createdAt-sorted index descending (scanForward: false) for each status partition and takes the max across statuses — not the base table, whose sort key is ticketId, not recency
npx tsc --noEmit passes in the sandbox

evals.name: status-counts
evals.prompt: You are working in an existing TypeScript project (a helpdesk backend) that uses @faceteer/facet with DynamoDB Local already running on localhost:8000. Read README.md and src/facets.ts first. Implement src/counts.ts exporting `getStatusCounts(orgId: string): Promise<{ open: number; pending: number; closed: number }>` counting the org's tickets per status. The org may have far more tickets than fit in one query page. Then run `npx tsx setup-table.ts` and `npx tsx seed.ts`, and write and run demo-counts.ts printing the result for org 'acme'. Typecheck with `npx tsc --noEmit`.
assertions: Demo output shows open: 100, pending: 100, closed: 100
Each status query supplies BOTH orgId and status to the byStatusCreated index (no partial-partition-key query), and pagination loops while a cursor is returned
npx tsc --noEmit passes in the sandbox

evals.name: import-fixture-dedup
evals.prompt: You are working in an existing TypeScript project (a helpdesk backend) that uses @faceteer/facet with DynamoDB Local already running on localhost:8000. Read README.md and src/facets.ts first. Implement src/import.ts exporting `importTickets(tickets: Ticket[]): Promise<{ written: number; failedTicketIds: string[] }>` where `written` is the number of tickets actually persisted to DynamoDB and `failedTicketIds` lists tickets that failed to persist — a caller must be able to trust both numbers. Then run `npx tsx setup-table.ts`, and write and run demo-import.ts that loads the 60 entries from import-fixture.json (in the project root; its date fields are ISO strings, so parse them into the Ticket shape), imports them, and prints the result. Typecheck with `npx tsc --noEmit`.
assertions: Demo output reports written: 58 and failedTicketIds: [] (the fixture contains 60 entries but two are duplicate ticketIds within the same partition, which DynamoDB batch writes collapse)
Failures are detected from the batch put result (failed / hasFailures / put arrays), not from try/catch, and never by zipping input order against result order
npx tsc --noEmit passes in the sandbox

evals.name: session-ttl-string
evals.prompt: You are working in an existing TypeScript project (a helpdesk backend) that uses @faceteer/facet with DynamoDB Local already running on localhost:8000. Read README.md and src/facets.ts first. Our public API exchanges sessions as JSON: { sessionId: string; userId: string; createdAt: string; expiresAt: string } where createdAt/expiresAt are ISO-8601 strings. Create src/session.ts with a Zod-validated Session model matching that contract, a SessionFacet keyed only by sessionId, configured so DynamoDB automatically deletes each session once its expiresAt passes, and an exported `createSession(userId: string): Promise<Session>` that writes a session expiring 24 hours from now and returns it, throwing if the write failed. Then run `npx tsx setup-table.ts`, and write and run demo-session.ts that creates a session, fetches it back with SessionFacet.get, and prints it. Typecheck with `npx tsc --noEmit`.
assertions: The raw DynamoDB item's ttl attribute is an N-type epoch-seconds value within 15 minutes of now+86400 — not a 1970-era number produced by parseInt on an ISO string, and not absent
The session read back via SessionFacet.get matches what createSession returned (validator handles the stored representation)
createSession inspects the put result (wasSuccessful) and throws on failure
npx tsc --noEmit passes in the sandbox
